analyst_view.overall: Brighton (5th of 36, 7 points) host Universitatea Craiova (8th, also 7 points) in a game that matters for a top-eight finish for both. Brighton were second in the Premier League at the international break after six clean-sheet wins in seven league games, and they won 1-0 at Getafe in this competition. They play Newcastle three days later, rotate a lot in Europe, and a team-news site lists Tzimas, Ferguson, Mitoma, Azeez and Yohanna out, with Minteh and Hadjam doubtful; none of these are in the numbers' missing list. Craiova, under Filipe Coelho, have named the same eleven in recent games and report no absences. No referee is named yet. I lean a little lower on Brighton's attacking numbers because of the absences and rotation.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.5 goals, 2.9 of them for Brighton, and they already take a little off for Brighton scoring only 4 in their last six. With Mitoma, Ferguson and Tzimas reported out and a rotated side likely before Newcastle, I take off 5%, to about 3.3 goals. Craiova's settled defence held Getafe to 1-1.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.7 corners, 8.3 of them for Brighton. Even a changed Brighton side will keep the ball and push Craiova back, so I see no reason to move this. I stay at 10.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards, with Craiova (2.5) expected to collect more chasing the game; their recent card counts are already in. No referee has been named yet. I stay at 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.9 shots, 22 of them Brighton's, and they already add a little for Brighton's recent shot volume. Missing several attackers and likely to rotate, Brighton should create a bit less, so I take off 4%, to about 27.7 shots.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target and already take 7% off Brighton's side for poor recent accuracy. The absences of Mitoma and the strikers Ferguson and Tzimas point the same way, so I take off a further 4%, to about 10.0.
